title: A world's stored scripts v1: the list (world.scripts.v1), a refusal, the reports and a done
rule: A code's number and retry are never changed, and a number is never used again. A limit is stated in the list and in the refusal it causes.

codes.name: refused-module
codes.means: The module check refused the bytes. The detail is the refusal and the byte it is about.

codes.name: bad-face
codes.means: The module's face answered out of range: its version, its state's place or size, or its slot count.

codes.name: not-stored
codes.means: The world has stored no module of this hash. Store the module, then name it.

codes.name: withdrawn
codes.means: The module is switched off everywhere. It is not served, and no new edit names it. The words say why.

codes.name: grows
codes.means: A publish adds a script, or lets a script do more than the live one: a handler, a power or a call. Nothing was published. Repeat it with the hashes listed, to confirm each.

codes.name: store-full
codes.means: The world stores as many modules as it may. A module no revision names is collected a day after it was stored.

codes.name: rate
codes.means: The author's daily limit for this is spent. The answer says the limit and when it lifts.

codes.name: no-compiler
codes.means: This server compiles no source. Build the module with coax/web/script.sh and store its bytes.

codes.name: refused-source
codes.means: The compile job refused the source. The words are the compiler's, or the job's limit that was reached.

codes.name: bad-request
codes.means: The request is not one this route takes: a name, a hash, a reason or a body that does not read.
